item.text:
Research continuation completed for all eight selected chapters. No scores, score ranges, rankings, or judge-directed advice were produced.

The repository and manifest could not be persisted: the managed read-only sandbox failed every filesystem operation with `bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`. The entries below are copy-ready for `research-ledger-manifest.json`.

### 1B — Catastrophic and existential risk

Rechecked contrary searches for nuclear, biological, cyber, dual-use, and crisis conduct. No additional Buhari-specific 2022 misuse, concealment, command, crisis, proliferation, or independent audit evidence was recovered.

Existing E019 and E023–E047 remain usable with their current dispositions and mappings. The chapter remains evidence-rich on formal policy and institutional activity, but operational attribution is unresolved.

### 2B — International peace and lawful security

- **E048** — Buhari publicly directed security agencies to remain alert during October 2022 Abuja terror warnings and expressed confidence in ongoing military and intelligence efforts. Direct presidential statement; target-period. Contrary evidence: this is an assurance, not an independent outcome audit. Mappings: `2B.2`, `2B.3`, `2B.6`, `2B.10`. [State House, lines in October 28 statement](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-buhari-to-security-agencies-all-persons-be-alert-dont-panic/)

- **E049** — The Defence Ministry reported that September 2022 military operations were conducted under Buhari’s Commander-in-Chief directive and claimed thousands of Boko Haram members laid down arms. Official operational claim; target-period. Attribution is direct for the directive, but outcomes remain self-reported. Contrary evidence: continuing insurgency and civilian-protection concerns. Mappings: `2B.1`, `2B.3`, `2B.6`, `2B.7`. [Defence Ministry](https://defence.gov.ng/2022/09/10/security-minister-of-defence-commends-military-performance-as-over-3407-bht-laid-down-arms/)

- **E050** — The Kuje custodial-centre attack occurred on 5 July 2022 despite the presence of military, police, intelligence, immigration, and correctional personnel. Institutional failure context; no personal Buhari order established. Mappings: `2B.3`, `2B.6`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`. [Nigerian Correctional Service](https://www.corrections.gov.ng/news/update%3A-attack-on-kuje-custodial-centre?news_id=29)

- **E051** — The President urged the Army’s 2022 conference to improve human-rights compliance and information gathering during operations. Direct target-period presidential direction. Contrary evidence: the statement does not demonstrate compliance or remedy. Mappings: `2B.3`, `2B.6`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`. [State House](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-buhari-canvasses-army-neutrality-on-2023-polls-wants-human-rights-obligations-sustained/)

- **E052** — The Federal Ministry of Information stated in April 2022 that the Buhari administration was pursuing police–community cooperation and justice for victims of crime. Official claim; weak independent verification. Mappings: `2B.6`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`. [Federal Ministry of Information](https://fmino.gov.ng/dingyadi-charges-communities-to-cooperate-with-npf-to-tackle-banditry-terrorism/)

Shortfall remains: no independent operational-order record or conclusive personal accountability finding.

### 3B — Domestic safety and protection

- **E053** — NHRC monitored detention facilities in Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe and sought immediate redress for unlawfully detained displaced persons. Target-period institutional protection activity; not Buhari-specific. Mappings: `3B.6`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.10`. [NHRC 2022 Annual Report, pp. 58–59](https://nhrc.gov.ng/files/publications/Annual_Report/2022%20ANNUAL%20REPORT%20FINAL%20FINAL%20docx%20%281%29.pdf)

- **E054** — NHRC conducted a nationwide audit of correctional and detention facilities in 2022 to assess compliance and generate recommendations for government intervention. Independent oversight evidence; implementation of recommendations remains unresolved. Mappings: `3B.6`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.10`. [NHRC 2022 Annual Report, p. 59](https://nhrc.gov.ng/files/publications/Annual_Report/2022%20ANNUAL%20REPORT%20FINAL%20FINAL%20docx%20%281%29.pdf)

- **E055** — The NHRC’s SARS panel heard 295 petitions, indicted 72 police officers, recommended prosecution or discipline, and awarded compensation to 100 petitioners in September 2022. Strong target-period remedy evidence; federal presidential responsibility is indirect. Mappings: `3B.6`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`. [NHRC Annual Report, pp. 59–60](https://nhrc.gov.ng/files/publications/Annual_Report/2022%20ANNUAL%20REPORT%20FINAL%20FINAL%20docx%20%281%29.pdf)

- **E056** — The NHRC and UNDP supported transitional-justice work in Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe, including 70 community cases. Positive remedy and reconciliation mechanism; effectiveness and federal ownership remain limited. Mappings: `3B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`. [NHRC Annual Report, p. 60](https://nhrc.gov.ng/files/publications/Annual_Report/2022%20ANNUAL%20REPORT%20FINAL%20FINAL%20docx%20%281%29.pdf)

- **E057** — The U.S. 2022 human-rights report identified unlawful killings, torture, arbitrary detention, civilian harm, media restrictions, and weak accountability, while noting that some security personnel were sometimes investigated. Independent adverse and contrary evidence. Mappings: `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.6`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.10`. [U.S. State Department report, lines 41 onward](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089140.html)

Shortfall remains: no direct Buhari order, knowledge, or personal responsibility finding for most abuses.

### 4B — Political freedom and authoritarian restraint

- **E058** — The Senate rejected Buhari’s requested Electoral Act amendment on 9 March 2022 after a court order barred tampering with the newly enacted law. Direct evidence of legislative and judicial constraint. Mappings: `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`, `4B.10`. [National Assembly, lines 43–73](https://nass.gov.ng/news/item/1633)

- **E059** — BTI reported that citizens and media could express criticism, private media retained substantial autonomy, and courts often ruled for media, while state-security harassment and executive dominance weakened checks and balances. Independent mixed evidence, though its coverage period is broader than 2022. Mappings: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.7`. [BTI 2022, pp. 8–10](https://www.ecoi.net/en/file/local/2069641/country_report_2022_NGA.pdf)

- **E060** — Freedom House found Nigeria’s online space diverse and politically pluralistic, with robust government-supporting and opposition debate. Contrary evidence against treating the information environment as uniformly closed. Mappings: `4B.1`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`. [Freedom House Freedom on the Net 2022](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2022)

- **E061** — Freedom House reported that government agencies ignored civil-society information requests about security access to identity databases in March 2022 and that judicial access-to-information remedies were rare. Target-period adverse institutional evidence. Mappings: `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.7`. [Freedom House, lines 327–331](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2022)

- **E062** — Buhari endorsed a National Peace Committee initiative for issue-based, peaceful, and transparent 2023 campaigning in September 2022. Direct presidential rhetoric and succession-period process evidence; implementation not established. Mappings: `4B.1`, `4B.4`, `4B.10`. [State House](https://statehouse.gov.ng/2023-president-buhari-wants-issue-based-campaigns-urges-political-actors-to-shun-personal-attacks-incitements/)

Shortfall remains: no comprehensive 2022 opposition-treatment or electoral-implementation audit.

### 5B — Economic well-being

- **E063** — The Budget Office page confirms that first-, second-, third-, and fourth-quarter 2022 budget implementation reports exist and that the office implements federal budget and fiscal policy. Gateway recovery; report contents were not exposed in the HTML. Disposition: `context`, not final evidence. Mappings: `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`, `8B.3`, `8B.4`. [Budget Office, lines 66–112](https://budgetoffice.gov.ng/index.php/resources/internal-resources/reports/quarterly-budget-implementation/2022-budget-implementation-report)

- **E064** — The World Bank described Nigeria’s December 2022 economic position as challenging and deteriorating, requiring macroeconomic, competitiveness, and social-protection reforms. Independent target-period assessment. Mappings: `5B.1`, `5B.4`, `5B.7`, `5B.8`, `5B.10`. [World Bank NDU](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/74e2f8585c426106f79f30a7b5fbc879-0360012022/nigeria-development-update-ndu-december-2022)

- **E065** — The World Bank reported 2021 revenue at only 7% of GDP and linked low spending to poor development outcomes. Target-period external assessment of inherited/current fiscal performance. Mappings: `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`. [World Bank, lines 189–191, 230–234](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2022/11/21/nigeria-needs-to-spend-more-and-better)

- **E066** — The World Bank reported that subsidies were inefficient and regressive, with the poorest 40% consuming only 3% of subsidized petrol. Strong distributional evidence; not personal intent evidence. Mappings: `5B.2`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`. [World Bank, lines 246–248](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2022/11/21/nigeria-needs-to-spend-more-and-better)

- **E067** — The World Bank reported very low social-sector spending, weak human capital, and constrained fiscal space caused by salaries, pensions, and interest payments. Mappings: `5B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`, `6B.1`, `6B.3`. [World Bank, lines 230–247](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2022/11/21/nigeria-needs-to-spend-more-and-better)

Shortfall remains: precise execution tables, appointments, procurement, and correction decisions were not recovered.

### 6B — Social well-being

- **E068** — The World Bank Poverty Assessment explicitly analyzed poverty, inequality, labour markets, climate shocks, social protection, fuel subsidies, and state-level variation, while warning that linking macroeconomic and household outcomes is difficult. Mappings: `6B.1`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`. [World Bank Poverty Assessment](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/nigeria/publication/afw-nigeria-poverty-assessment)

- **E069** — The World Bank reported that low public spending reduced the quantity and quality of health and education services and left Nigeria with very low human capital. Mappings: `6B.1`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`. [World Bank, lines 230–234](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2022/11/21/nigeria-needs-to-spend-more-and-better)

- **E070** — NHRC monitoring in the Northeast included detention visits, protection-data collection, awareness activities, and immediate-redress efforts for displaced persons. Mappings: `6B.6`, `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`. [NHRC Annual Report, pp. 58–59](https://nhrc.gov.ng/files/publications/Annual_Report/2022%20ANNUAL%20REPORT%20FINAL%20FINAL%20docx%20%281%29.pdf)

- **E071** — The World Bank’s state-level approach confirms that Nigeria’s federal structure materially complicates attribution of poverty and service outcomes. This is an attribution-limiting unit, not negative ruler evidence. Mappings: `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.10`. [World Bank Poverty Assessment, lines 49–53](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/nigeria/publication/afw-nigeria-poverty-assessment)

Shortfall remains: no Buhari-owned program-to-beneficiary chain or independent 2022 service-quality audit was recovered.

### 7B — Personal integrity

- **E072** — Buhari instructed the EFCC to avoid partisan political use, endorsed standard operating procedures, and called for rules-based enforcement. Direct target-period statement; official/self-reported and therefore limited. Mappings: `7B.5`, `7B.6`, `7B.7`, `7B.8`, `7B.10`. [State House, lines 23–45](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-buhari-cautions-efcc-on-political-interference-commends-recovery-of-looted-funds/)

- **E073** — The same official account claimed 2,220 convictions and recovery of more than ₦152 billion and $385 million within one year. Institutional performance claim, not independent proof and not personal benefit evidence. Mappings: `7B.5`, `7B.7`, `7B.8`. [State House, lines 27–37](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-buhari-cautions-efcc-on-political-interference-commends-recovery-of-looted-funds/)

- **E074** — SERAP filed a 2022 suit seeking to compel Buhari to investigate alleged missing ecological funds and recover public money. This is a documented scrutiny event and allegation, not a finding of personal corruption. Mappings: `7B.5`, `7B.7`, `7B.8`, `7B.9`. [The Guardian, lines 164–183](https://guardian.ng/news/serap-sues-buhari-over-failure-to-probe-alleged-missing-trillions-in-ecological-funds/)

The personal-integrity nexus remains unresolved. No reliable 2022 asset declaration, family-benefit record, procurement-conflict finding, or personal enrichment evidence was recovered.

### 8B — Effectiveness and competence

- **E075** — Buhari’s October 2022 performance-review address established a formal delivery-monitoring system: quarterly reports for 29 ministries, weekly updates from the Secretary to the Government, and review against 2023 benchmarks. Direct target-period governance-process evidence. Mappings: `8B.2`, `8B.3`, `8B.4`, `8B.5`, `8B.7`, `8B.10`. [State House, lines 23–38](https://statehouse.gov.ng/address-by-president-buhari-at-the-3rd-ministerial-performance-review-retreat/)

- **E076** — The same address claimed completion or substantial progress on rail, roads, airports, broadband, and other infrastructure. Official achievement claim; independent outcome verification remains incomplete. Mappings: `8B.3`, `8B.4`, `8B.6`, `8B.9`. [State House, lines 39–48](https://statehouse.gov.ng/address-by-president-buhari-at-the-3rd-ministerial-performance-review-retreat/)

- **E077** — Buhari explicitly framed the October retreat as a final review before the May 2023 handover and described the delivery unit as a legacy mechanism for his successor. Direct succession and institutional-continuity evidence. Mappings: `8B.5`, `8B.7`, `8B.9`, `8B.10`. [State House, lines 30–38, 80](https://statehouse.gov.ng/address-by-president-buhari-at-the-3rd-ministerial-performance-review-retreat/)

- **E078** — The World Bank’s December 2022 assessment found deteriorating economic conditions and required reforms in macroeconomic stability, competitiveness, and social protection. Independent contrary evidence against treating official delivery claims as sufficient outcomes. Mappings: `8B.1`, `8B.3`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.9`. [World Bank NDU](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/74e2f8585c426106f79f30a7b5fbc879-0360012022/nigeria-development-update-ndu-december-2022)

- **E079** — NHRC’s 2022 investigative panel produced recommendations, disciplinary referrals, compensation, detention audits, and transitional-justice mechanisms. This supports the existence of corrective institutions but not Buhari’s personal effectiveness in enforcing them. Mappings: `8B.4`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.8`, `8B.10`. [NHRC Annual Report](https://nhrc.gov.ng/files/publications/Annual_Report/2022%20ANNUAL%20REPORT%20FINAL%20FINAL%20docx%20%281%29.pdf)

Shortfall remains: no independent portfolio-wide evaluation, personnel-quality record, or durable-outcome audit.
